Ambrook helps American family-run businesses become more profitable and resilient.
From volatile markets to climate shifts, independent operators face mounting pressure. While sustainable investments often yield the best long-term returns, they require financial clarity and capital that fragmented legacy systems can’t provide.

We are rebuilding the financial infrastructure that real economy operators rely on. By replacing paperwork with modern tools for accounting, banking, and spending, Ambrook gives owners the data they need to prove viability to lenders and the next generation. We empower the stewards of land and labor to make confident investments in their future.

We’re a Series B startup backed by Lachy Groom, Thrive Capital, Dylan Field, Thomson Reuters Ventures, Cameron Ventures, and leaders at Notion, Gusto, and Vercel. We’re looking for team members to help us untangle the intersection of American industry, climate, and the economy.



The Opportunity

This posting is for the spring co-op cycle, for at least 6 months from January through June 2027.

As part of our engineering co-op program, you'll work as a valued member of our team building features that directly impact farmers across America. This is an exciting opportunity to gain real-world development experience while contributing to sustainable agriculture, with mentorship from experienced engineers who are invested in your growth.

You'll also get real reps with modern AI dev tooling and with building AI products themselves. We've used AI dev tools since the earliest days of the company and stay close to the bleeding edge. Through Ambrook Labs, we're exploring AI-native features like natural language invoice drafting, voice-driven bookkeeping entry, and Desk, a task inbox that turns unstructured voice and text into organized workflows. We also speak regularly about the impact AI is having on us as people and developers, and balance marvel & enthusiasm about these tools with a respect for our craft.



We’re looking for someone who we can count on to…

 - Own: Build and ship real product features that customers use, while helping improve our infrastructure alongside experienced engineers.

 - Learn: Gain experience in engineering best practices, agile development, and working across teams while discovering how agtech and climate solutions help farmers succeed.

 - Grow: Understand the basics of agricultural finance, farm operations, and sustainability practices through hands-on project work, including how real-world financial data actually looks and how AI can help make sense of it.

 - Contribute: Help identify ways to improve our development process and codebase while learning full-stack development.



Within the first few weeks you’ll

 - Learn how to use Ambrook’s tech stack to deliver a standalone feature to our customers

 - Contribute to Engineering team meetings and review code from peers. 

 - Analyze Ambrook’s use of best practices and share a technical note with our team about where we have opportunities to improve.



By the end of your co-op you’ll…

 - Collaborate with the team on core product work.

 - Own a project from start to finish - from a technical design document through implementation. As the engineering owner, you’ll break down your project into granular pieces and practice good project management hygiene, triaging and prioritizing new issues that come in.

 - Collaborate with our Product team to influence prioritization of feature ideas and requests with insights from our audience.

 - Embed yourself deeply in understanding the state of farm finance, building a strong intuition about customer needs and audience segmentation.



About you

 - Currently pursuing B.S. (or higher) in Computer Science or a related field. Expected graduation: Spring 2028.

 - Available to work full-time in our NYC office for the spring co-op cycle, for at least 6 months from January through June 2027.

 - Excited to build software that makes natural resource industries like agriculture more sustainable and profitable.

 - Comfortable taking on ambiguous problems and creating elegant technical solutions.

 - Exhibit strong computer science fundamentals and an eagerness to learn.

 - Know when AI coding tools can expedite your workflows, and also when you need to dive into the code yourself.

 - Experience with TypeScript, React, React Native, and/or Next.js.

 - Bonus: Experience with LLM APIs, prompt engineering, or basic ML tooling.

 - Bonus: Experience in agriculture.



Our tech stack

 - Next.js / React application written in TypeScript

 - Hosted on Google Cloud

 - Firestore & Postgres & Google Cloud Storage for data storage

 - BigQuery & Data Studio for data insights



What makes this co-op special

 - Make a real difference: Build features that help farmers adopt sustainable practices and grow their businesses.

 - Experience life at a high-growth startup: See the complete product development cycle from design to deployment in a fast-paced environment.

 - Get personalized mentorship: Work directly with senior engineers who are invested in your growth.

 - Join a mission-driven team: Experience startup culture while helping build the future of sustainable agriculture.

 - Work closely with customers: Your work will help real farms and agribusinesses across America succeed - and you'll get to meet some of them.



Values

 - Real Talk – We create space for ourselves and others to be straightforward, vulnerable, and accountable.

 - Reach Understanding – We are driven by curiosity and empathy to learn about our customers, team, and world.

 - Be Proactively Resourceful – We are internally motivated and externally empowered to identify opportunities and solve problems.

 - Derisk Thoughtfully – We lean into the biggest risks we face as a company and put in the work to address them systematically.

 - Find the Positive-Sum – We believe in creating incentive structures that align the needs of our company, our customers, and our planet. 



Ambrook is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building diversity and inclusion into our core company culture.

Ambrook can support visa sponsorship (OPT/CPT, TN, J-1) for eligible candidates.

At Armadin, we're a group of engineers, researchers, and security researchers on a mission to redefine what proactive security can do in the AI era. Cyberattacks are becoming autonomous and relentless and we believe defending against threats before they materialize is one of the most powerful ways to protect the institutions the world depends on.



We're building autonomous proactive security from the ground up, reinforcing the tradecraft of elite security practioners into purpose-built security models and agents that discover risk and remediate it before organizations are breached.



Led by Kevin Mandia, founder of Mandiant ($5.4B exit to Google), our team brings together researchers and engineers from Google, xAI, Meta, Stanford, Georgia Tech, Waterloo, Berkeley, and MIT to reinvent security for an adversary that never sleeps.



The Role

As a Software Engineer Intern on the Agent Platform team, you'll help build the orchestration and reasoning systems that let our security agents operate independently at scale — investigating, triaging, and remediating risk with the judgment of an elite red teamer. You'll ship production code alongside full-time engineers from day one, paired with a mentor invested in your growth, and see your work deployed against real adversaries rather than left in a sandbox.



We're a small, fast-moving team, so interns get real ownership: you'll work across the stack, from distributed backend systems to the evaluation harnesses that keep autonomous agents safe and reliable, and you'll partner directly with founders, researchers, and customer-facing engineers to understand the problems worth solving.

 - Design and build components of our agentic orchestration platform. The systems that let autonomous security agents plan, act, and self-correct.

 - Contribute production code to core services, balancing latency, cost, and reliability at scale.

 - Build evaluation and observability tooling to measure and improve non-deterministic agent behavior.

 - Pair with a dedicated mentor and collaborate with engineers, researchers, and threat-intel experts to ship features end-to-end.

 - Participate in design reviews, code reviews, and team rituals just like a full-time engineer.

 

Required

 - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Math, or a related technical field, with an expected graduation in 2027 or 2028.

 - Comfortable writing clean, well-tested code and picking up new languages and frameworks quickly.

 - Solid foundation in data structures, algorithms, and distributed systems fundamentals.

 - Prior experience with Python, Go, or with LLM/agent frameworks is a plus.

 

Nice to Have

 - Experience with data visualization or graph rendering (D3 or similar).

 - Exposure to building products that emphasize reliability and scalability.

 - Open-source contributions, hackathon projects, or independent builds that show initiative.

 

Technologies We Use 

 - Our stack centers on Python and Go for backend services, React for front-end tooling, and a mix of open-source and in-house infrastructure to orchestrate and evaluate LLM-driven agents.

About Niantic Spatial

At Niantic Spatial, we're building the future of physical AI. Powered by a proprietary database of over 30 billion posed images, our groundbreaking mapping technology unlocks a new dimension of interaction and spatial intelligence that helps both humans and machines better understand, represent, navigate, and engage with the real environment.

Our reconstruction technology captures environments with geometric accuracy and extreme detail from any standard camera, and our Visual Positioning System delivers precise positioning almost anywhere in the world. We serve customers across robotics, the public sector, and energy and industrial markets - building for the 80% of economic activity that takes place beyond our screens.



About the Role

We're hiring software engineering interns for Summer 2027; each intern will be embedded in a specialized track. You won't be shadowing or running demos - you'll own a real problem on a small team, write code that ships to production, and work on systems and datasets that don't exist anywhere else: petabyte-scale 3D reconstructions, foundation models trained on physical space, and positioning infrastructure deployed globally.

Select your primary track when you apply. We'll match you based on fit; switching tracks after matching is uncommon but possible if there's strong mutual interest.



Track 1: ML /AI Infrastructure

You'll build the systems that make large-scale physical AI possible. Not just run experiments, but design the distributed training pipelines, data ingestion infrastructure, and GPU optimization layers that let us train foundation models on billions of images and 3D data points.

 - Model Training with PyTorch — Implement, train, and evaluate model architectures in PyTorch, iterating on data loaders, loss functions, and training loops to improve model quality and convergence on real production datasets.

 - Training Infrastructure — Design and scale distributed training pipelines for our Large Geospatial Model, handling petabyte-scale spatial data across multi-GPU and multi-node environments.

 - Data Pipelines — Build high-throughput ingestion and preprocessing pipelines that transform raw imagery and 3D point clouds into training-ready datasets.

 - Observability — Instrument training runs with metrics, dashboards, and alerting so engineering teams can debug and iterate faster.

Best for: Students obsessed with the intersection of ML and systems - PyTorch, distributed computing (Ray, Spark), CUDA, and high-performance architecture.



Track 2: Product Engineering

You'll build the product APIs and services that sit behind our spatial computing products, helping customers manage projects, organize spatial data, upload content, and turn it into useful experiences. You'll work across backend and product engineering to take features from design to production, with a focus on clear interfaces, reliable workflows, and software that other teams can build on.

 - Product Features — Build and ship features for managing organizations, projects, spatial data, and content.

 - API Design — Design the interfaces that connect our products, web and mobile applications, and developer tools, making them consistent, well-documented, and easy to use.

 - Workflows & Integrations — Connect the steps behind core product workflows, from uploading and processing data to making results available to users and applications.

 - End-to-End Delivery — Collaborate with engineers across frontend, backend, and infrastructure to launch features and learn from real customer use.

Best for: Students who enjoy building products from the backend up and interested in how APIs and data power user experiences. Motivated by shipping software that real customers and developers use.



Track 3: Backend Systems

You'll build and harden the high-throughput services that power our Visual Positioning System and reconstruction platform - processing vast volumes of visual data and delivering centimeter-level positioning to users and robots globally.

 - Service Development — Design and ship microservices in Go or C++ that sit in the critical path of our positioning and reconstruction APIs.

 - Data Ingestion — Build and optimize pipelines that ingest, validate, and route large volumes of visual and sensor data from diverse hardware sources.

 - Performance & Reliability — Profile service bottlenecks, improve latency, and improve system observability through structured logging, metrics, and distributed tracing.

 - API Design — Contribute to internal and external API design, writing clean, well-tested, production-grade interfaces that other teams and customers depend on.

Best for: Pragmatic engineers who care about correctness, performance, and clean systems design and want to see their code serving real traffic within weeks.



What You'll Bring (All Tracks)

 - Currently pursuing a BS or MS in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Computer Vision, or a related field.

 - TypeScript, Python, C++ or Go experience for Infrastructure and Backend tracks.

 - Genuine curiosity about how AI interacts with the physical world - 3D reconstruction, spatial reasoning, or real-world positioning systems.

 - Ability to work independently, debug ambiguous problems, and communicate clearly with a small team.

 - Available for 4 days per week in our San Francisco office for the full 12-week internship.

Nice to Have

 - Experience with cloud infrastructure - Kubernetes, AWS or GCP, Docker, Terraform.

 - Familiarity with CUDA or GPU parallelization.

 - Open-source contributions to libraries like PyTorch, OpenCV, COLMAP, or similar.

 - Prior work in robotics, autonomous systems, XR, or spatial computing (coursework, research, or projects acceptable)

 - Exposure to Gaussian Splatting, NeRF, or 3D reconstruction techniques

 - Familiarity with REST APIs

 - Experience with SQL or other relational databases

 - Experience using AI-assisted development tools (Claude, ChatGPT, etc.) to write, debug, and improve code



Compensation & Benefits

The expected hourly rate for this internship is 48–70/hour, based on assessed skills, experience, and relevant coursework. Housing assistance is available for candidates outside the Bay Area - details provided during the offer process.



Location & Work Model

This internship is based in our San Francisco, CA office. We work in a high-collaboration environment and ask interns to be on-site a minimum of 4 days per week. To make that easy, we provide lunch every day and snacks are always stocked.

We know the strongest candidates don't always tick every box. If you're excited about this role and believe you could do it well, we encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't match every qualification listed - you may be exactly who we're looking for.

ABOUT REVEL

At Revel, we are revolutionizing the way the world’s most critical hardware is controlled—across aerospace, automotive, energy, and manufacturing sectors. Our next-generation software stack combines an intuitive command/control interface, a specialized programming language tailored for hardware control, and a high-performance runtime environment. We empower engineers to build, test, and deploy critical systems rapidly, reliably, and safely.

 


THE INTERNSHIP

As an Embedded Software Engineering Intern at Revel, you’ll work on the software that connects our high-performance runtime to the physical world.

You’ll work closely with experienced software and embedded engineers to develop systems software, integrate with hardware, and build the foundations that allow Revel to reliably control complex industrial machinery. You’ll gain hands-on experience working across the boundary between software and hardware—from communication protocols and hardware interfaces to Linux systems and low-level debugging.

This is a highly technical internship for students who want to understand what happens below the application layer and build software where performance, reliability, and correctness matter.

You’ll contribute to real engineering projects, learn from senior engineers, and develop experience with the systems programming and hardware integration challenges behind critical software.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Write and contribute to Rust code targeting Linux userspace

 - Support the integration of industrial hardware and learn to work with register maps and hardware communication protocols

 - Contribute to Hardware Abstraction Layers (HALs) that allow Revel software to interface with physical hardware

 - Develop software that communicates with sensors, actuators, controllers, and other hardware

 - Learn and use hardware debugging tools such as logic analyzers and oscilloscopes

 - Write tests and contribute to improving the reliability and quality of low-level software

 - Participate in code reviews and collaborate with experienced software and embedded engineers

 - Debug issues across software, operating systems, communication interfaces, and hardware

 - Build an understanding of how reliability and correctness become critical requirements in real-world systems

 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field

 - Rising Junior or Senior graduating in 2027 or 2028

 - Strong programming fundamentals and experience with C, C++, Rust, or another systems-oriented language

 - Foundational understanding of operating systems, computer architecture, or Linux

 - Interest in understanding how software interacts with hardware at a low level

 - Strong analytical and debugging skills

 - Hands-on experience through coursework, personal projects, research, or previous internships

 - Curious, self-directed, and excited to learn from experienced engineers

 - Comfortable working in a fast-paced, technically challenging environment

 - Strong written and verbal communication skills

 - US citizen, lawful permanent resident, refugee, or asylee (ITAR requirement)

 


BONUS POINTS

 - Coursework or personal projects involving embedded systems, microcontrollers, or firmware

 - Experience with Rust, particularly through personal or academic projects

 - Familiarity with communication protocols such as SPI, I2C, UART, or CAN

 - Experience working with Linux internals, operating systems, or low-level networking

 - Experience with hardware debugging tools such as logic analyzers or oscilloscopes

 - Experience working with sensors, actuators, development boards, or other physical hardware

 - Interest in real-time, safety-critical, or high-reliability systems

 - Experience building projects that bridge software and hardware

 - Experience with robotics, aerospace, automotive, industrial automation, or other hardware-focused applications

 


WHY REVEL

 - Work on software that controls real hardware — build systems that interact directly with the physical world

 - Go deep technically — work at the intersection of systems programming, hardware, and software

 - Learn from exceptional engineers — work closely with engineers who have built critical software systems

 - Build real things — contribute to production software rather than purely academic or experimental projects

 - Take on meaningful problems — work on technology used by customers across aerospace, automotive, energy, and advanced manufacturing

 - Grow quickly — work in a small, ambitious team where your contributions are visible and your learning curve is steep

 


INTERNSHIP DETAILS

 - Program: Summer 2027 Internship

 - Duration: June - August 2027

 - Type: Summer, paid internship

 - Location: Los Angeles or San Francisco

 - Work environment: On-site

 - Travel: Occasional travel to customer sites may be required

 

Join us to redefine what’s possible in software for hardware.

 

ITAR Requirements
To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. You will work with design verification engineers to develop tests, improve verification environments, analyze coverage, debug failures, and apply simulation and formal methods to assess whether designs meet their specifications.
This internship is intended for a student who is ready to go beyond running existing tests and contribute to verification strategy, reusable infrastructure, and difficult debug problems. You will own a scoped project with guidance from experienced engineers and deliver verification work in a usable state.
What you will do
Translate architectural, microarchitectural, interface, and product requirements into verification scenarios, test plans, coverage goals, and checkers.
Develop and maintain SystemVerilog and UVM testbench components, sequences, tests, monitors, scoreboards, functional coverage, and end-of-test checks.
Add directed, constrained-random, error-injection, compliance, stress, and corner-case tests for blocks, subsystems, or top-level functionality.
Configure and run simulations and regressions using project submission flows, manifests, plusargs, firmware images, and test definitions.
Debug failures by correlating logs, UVM messages, assertions, register reports, firmware output, and Verdi or DVE waveforms.
Triage regression failures, distinguish design issues from testbench or environment issues, reproduce failures, and communicate actionable root-cause analysis.
Analyze functional and code coverage, identify untested scenarios or coverage gaps, and propose targeted tests or verification improvements.
Write, review, and debug SystemVerilog assertions and coverage properties that capture design intent and interface behavior.
Support formal verification flows such as design compile, reset analysis, automatic property extraction, dead-code analysis, and formal property verification.
Create or improve Python, Tcl, or other automation that simplifies test generation, regression execution, result parsing, coverage analysis, or failure triage.
Collaborate with RTL design, firmware, emulation, physical design, and systems engineers to clarify assumptions and close verification issues.
Document test intent, debug findings, coverage status, known limitations, and handoff information; present the completed project and recommendations.
What you bring
Enrollment in a bachelor’s, master’s, or Ph.D. program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related field.
Coursework, research, or project experience in digital logic, computer architecture, ASIC/FPGA design, verification, embedded systems, or hardware/software integration.
Programming or verification experience with SystemVerilog, Verilog, C, C++, Python, or a comparable language.
Familiarity with digital design concepts, simulation, testbenches, interfaces, clocks, resets, registers, and debugging from waveforms or logs.
Familiarity with Linux development environments, Git, command-line tools, and technical documentation.
Ability to reason from a specification, investigate failures systematically, and communicate clear technical conclusions.
Strong ownership, curiosity, practical judgment, and willingness to collaborate across engineering functions.
Preferred qualifications
Experience with UVM components, sequences, virtual sequences, agents, monitors, scoreboards, reference models, or functional coverage.
Familiarity with SystemVerilog Assertions, constrained-random testing, coverage-driven verification, error injection, or compliance testing.
Exposure to verification IP and protocols such as PCIe, CXL, AXI, or other high-speed and control interfaces.
Experience with Verdi, DVE, VCS, Questa, Xcelium, VC Formal, or comparable simulation and formal tools.
Familiarity with formal concepts such as assumptions, assertions, covers, counterexamples, reset analysis, dead-code analysis, or automatic property extraction.
Experience managing regressions, parsing results, debugging intermittent failures, or running jobs on a compute cluster or CI system.
Internship experience and compensation
This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges from $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.
Equal opportunity

Who we are
Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.
Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.
Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.
This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.
We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.
If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.
What you’ll do
As an ML Intern on our team, you will help bridge the gap between high-level AI research and real-world physical actuation for our next-generation autonomous transport platforms. Working alongside senior engineers, you will contribute directly to production-grade models, real-time edge pipelines, and multi-sensor data systems that power our physical machines.
Collaborate with research engineers to prototype, evaluate, and test emerging Machine Learning and Deep Learning models for trajectory planning and autonomous behavior.
Help design and evaluate multimodal systems that integrate raw multi-sensor data (Cameras, LiDAR, Radar) to improve spatial-temporal perception.
Assist in developing interactive world models and simulation tools to re-simulate real-world driving logs and analyze vehicle trajectories.
Profile and optimize inference pipelines to help run complex models under low latency constraints on vehicle edge hardware.
Work with data engineering workflows to identify, curate, and structure rare, complex edge cases and long-tail scenarios from physical operations.
Partner with validation and QA teams to run model releases through simulated scenarios to catch performance regressions and track model behavior.
What we’re looking for
Currently pursuing a BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, or a related technical field.
Strong foundation in deep learning concepts and experience with modern frameworks like PyTorch or JAX (through coursework, research, or prior internships).
Hands-on programming experience in Python; familiarity with C++ is a plus.
Academic coursework, project experience, or research in one or more relevant domains: Computer Vision, Spatial-Temporal Modeling, Reinforcement Learning, Model Optimization, Model Evaluation, or Data Engineering.
Familiarity with robotics data structures or multi-sensor processing (Cameras, LiDAR, or Radar) is highly preferred.
A passion for solving complex, messy real-world engineering problems and deploying AI into physical systems.
Why join us
At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.
What else you need to know
This role is based in our San Francisco office. Atoms is a company driven by invention and continuous change - we are constantly reimagining our industries, building new products, and refining how we operate. We do our best work together. That’s why all of our office-based teams work onsite, five days a week.
Program Dates: Our internship is a 12-weeks program. Cohort sessions run as follows:
Winter 2027: January – April
Summer 2027: Late May – September
The base salary range for this role is $70.00 per hour.
Actual compensation will be determined on an individual basis and may vary depending on experience, skills, and qualifications.
Ready to join us as we serve those who serve others?

As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern at Lexington Medical, you will spend the summer on a running production line that builds a surgical stapler, tracking yield, downtime, and cycle time, and owning one process improvement project from concept through implementation. You will troubleshoot alongside the operators and technicians who run the line, bring your own analysis to production support meetings, and present your results to engineering leadership before you leave.
About Lexington Medical
Lexington Medical designs and manufactures AEON™ surgical stapling technology at our headquarters in Bedford, Massachusetts, just outside Boston. Our products are used in minimally invasive surgery, where precision, reliability, and quality matter every time. Because engineering, manufacturing, and quality work together under one roof, the people building and supporting our products are close to both the process and the decisions behind it.
About the Role
As a Manufacturing Engineering Intern at Lexington Medical, you will work alongside manufacturing engineering on an operating line producing AEON™ surgical stapling products. Day to day, you will monitor line performance, troubleshoot equipment and process issues in real time with operators and technicians, analyze process data for trends, and propose changes such as fixturing updates or workflow revisions. Alongside that, you will own one manufacturing improvement project end to end, aligning with Manufacturing, Engineering, and Quality as you go. Because all three groups work in the same building in Bedford, getting that alignment means walking down the hall rather than waiting on a meeting invite.
Responsibilities
Monitor line performance metrics, including yield, downtime, and cycle time.
Partner with operators and technicians to troubleshoot equipment and process issues in real time.
Perform repairs and maintenance on custom production equipment.
Participate in daily and weekly production support meetings.
Assess current processes for bottlenecks and inefficiencies and analyze process data to identify trends and improvement opportunities.
Generate solutions, such as fixturing updates or workflow changes, and present them to the larger manufacturing team.
Implement approved changes by training operators, commissioning equipment, or making other line changes as needed.
Own a manufacturing improvement project from concept through implementation and present the outcome to engineering leadership.
Qualifications
Currently enrolled at an accredited university in an undergraduate or graduate program in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a similar technical discipline.
CAD experience (SolidWorks or similar)
Your resume should show a demonstrated ability to build and debug mechanical or electromechanical assemblies, whether from coursework, a project team, a lab, or personal projects.
Comfortable working with hand tools, shop equipment, and production machinery on the floor.
Able to read mechanical drawings and work from SOPs and written work instructions.
Able to clearly communicate analysis and observations to engineering team.
Skills that are a plus:
Comfort analyzing data in Excel or a similar tool
Time on a build team such as Formula SAE, Baja, or robotics
What Success Looks Like
You have an understanding of your improvement project and have iterated on potential solutions.
You have aligned all stakeholders of your proposed change (Ex. Manufacturing, Engineering, and Quality).
By the end of the internship, the change is running on the line and you have presented the impact it has had to the engineering team.
Location & Work Arrangement
This position is based at our headquarters in Bedford, Massachusetts, in the Greater Boston area, and is an on-site role. The internship runs from June 2027 through August 2027, on-site five days per week.
Hourly Rate
$25—$35 USD

Project Summary
The overarching goal of this R25 application is to provide training to diverse high school and undergraduate
students who will work with supportive faculty mentors to understand how environmental chemical
exposures contribute to non-communicable diseases, and how hazard and/or exposure mitigation can
improve health. Program faculty come from a diverse range of disciplines: toxicology, endocrinology, cell and
molecular biology, veterinary and animal sciences, chemistry, epidemiology, chemical engineering, civil and
environmental engineering, and science communication. We will focus on recruiting women and individuals
from underrepresented groups to participate in this summer program, which includes three aims:
1) To involve high school age young women in introductory summer research experiences and recruit those
with an interest in participating in research projects or science communication projects. By partnering with the
local Girls Inc. organization, we will offer week-long introductory training programs for 9th grade girls from
diverse but underserved communities in Western MA. With 24-26 girls participating every year, we will use this
program to recruit 10th and 11th grade girls to participate in Aims 2 and 3.
2) To create a learning community focused on understanding how environmental chemical exposures
contribute to non-communicable diseases and develop scientific strategies to create solutions to these
challenging problems. High school and undergraduate students will work with UMass faculty to understand
how environmental chemical exposures contribute to non-communicable diseases, and how hazards and/or
exposures can be mitigated. Research will focus on one of these areas:
 • molecular and cellular models of diseases relevant to environmental chemical exposures;
 • characterizing chemical exposures and their association with human diseases;
 • understanding the effects of environmental chemicals on conditions such as cancer and metabolic
diseases;
 • creating solutions for exposures to hazardous environmental chemicals including use of green chemistry
 principles to avoid hazards entirely and pollution remediation when exposures cannot be avoided.
3) To train diverse participants in methods to communicate complex environmental health concepts in the
context of our learning community and in broader communities. High school and undergraduate students will
work to create science communication tools, aimed at educating a lay audience about one or more topic
addressed in the laboratories in Aim 2. Communication tools could include static or animated infographics,
informational videos, podcasts, or other social media tools.

This Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) site at the University of Minnesota Department of Computer Science and Engineering aims to support a diverse group of undergraduate students in human-centered research projects that leverage computer science to advance social good. The objectives of this project are to: (1) provide support for undergraduate research, especially for students that are underrepresented or have limited access at their home institutions; (2) facilitate mentorship from leading researchers in virtual reality, visualization, human-computer interaction, and human-robot interaction; (3) explicitly train students in research methods and immerse them in the culture of science, and (4) provide professional development opportunities to prepare students for graduate school and scientific careers. REU student projects will produce novel technologies, algorithms, and interaction techniques that can enrich and empower human experiences with computing systems.
To achieve these goals, the REU site will recruit at least 50% of the cohort from institutions with limited research opportunities, with a particular emphasis on supporting women, underrepresented minorities, and first generation college students. Participants will be immersed in highly collaborative research labs supervised by faculty with longstanding commitments to mentoring undergraduate researchers. To help students make the connection between computer science and advancing social good, all REU projects will be aligned with one or more of the Sustainable Development Goals established by the United Nations Foundation. Students will apply their computer science knowledge to address important societal problems such as implicit bias mitigation, addiction recovery, locating underwater trash, sorting recyclables, and motivating climate action. At the cohort level, students will participate in a program of social events, research training seminars, invited research talks, and professional development workshops scheduled throughout the summer to support their scholarly and professional growth.
This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

As a Research & Development Intern, you will have the opportunity to tap into your curiosity and collaborate with some of the most innovative people around the world. Here, you will make an impact by:
Leveraging expertise to support the development of new technologies, providing growth opportunities, in addition to supporting existing 3M products, businesses, and operations.

The Radiological Protection Division is devoted to protecting workers, members of the public, and the environment from hazards due to exposure to radioactive material. Our staff is concerned with the recognition, evaluation, and control of radiological hazards to permit the safe use and application of ionizing radiation at Argonne. Interns will learn how to provide operational health physics support that includes planning radiological work and implementing radiation protection standards and best practices.
The following skills will be developed:
Learn how to evaluate radiological hazards and implement appropriate controls through the development of a radiological work permit
Learn to use computer applications in dosimetry, shielding, and spectrometry ̈
Learn to implement ALARA principles in radiological work
Acquire knowledge and hands-on training on the use of state-of-the-art health physics instrumentation to perform measurement and analysis of ionizing radiation.
Shadow health physics personnel in all support areas on site to understand the unique hazards and challenges.
Education and Experience Requirements
This opportunity is open to any undergraduate or graduate student with relevant experience who meets the following criteria:
Currently enrolled in a nuclear engineering, health physics, or physics program (ABET accreditation preferred) full time. Graduate students are eligible to apply.
Completed one year of schooling with a grade point average of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
Must be at least 18 years old at the beginning of the internship.
Must be a U.S. citizen or Legal Permanent Resident at the time of application.
May be subject to a drug screening test prior to or during the internship.
Desired skills:
Knowledge of: health physics/radiation protection theory and practice; measurement and analysis techniques for ionizing radiation and radioactivity; ALARA principles; radiation protection standards; biological effects of radiation.
Proven oral and written skills to effectively communicate technical information to workers and management.
Ability to develop interpersonal relationships with researchers and field support personnel.
Additionally, students seeking this opportunity should show in their application:
A desire to participate in a dynamic work environment with competing deadlines and a combination of desk and fieldwork.
Ability to assist in difficult situations and keep composure and confidence.
Attention to detail and willingness to participate in documenting of reviews, walkthroughs, and meetings.
This position is intended to be conducted on-site, actual schedule will be determined upon hire.

Living our purpose by following all company SOPs at each workstation to help our Pharmacists and Technicians manage and improve patient health

Taking telephonic prescriptions from the prescriber, and calling the prescriber to clarify prescriptions or facilitate medication changes, where allowed by state regulation
Maintaining the highest level of self-awareness and providing in-the-moment coaching, training, and mentoring to pharmacy team members while sharing best practices
Completing basic inventory activities, as permitted by law, and as directed by the pharmacy leadership team, such as accurately putting away medication deliveries and completing cycle counts, returns-to-stocks, waiting bin inventories, etc.

Your Role: R&D Laboratory Intern
As an R&D Laboratory Intern at Elanco’s global headquarters in Indianapolis, you will contribute directly to our Research and Breakthrough Innovation and Technical Development organizations by performing hands-on laboratory work in support of new and existing animal health products. You will own the progress of an innovative project and work alongside scientists and engineers to design and execute experiments, generate and interpret data, and contribute to robust processes and products for companion and/or farm animals.
Interns may be placed in one of several teams, including but not limited to:
Synthetic Technical Development – Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient, Formulation, or Analytical
Biopharma Technical Development – Bioprocess Development, Formulation, or Analytical
Early Research Antibody Discovery
Your Responsibilities:
Design and execute hands-on experiments in an R&D laboratory (e.g., synthetic chemistry, formulation development, analytical development, upstream/downstream bioprocess development, cell culture, immunoassays, molecular biology, or protein sciences), following established safety protocols and guidelines.
Prepare solutions, reagents, media, and test articles. Operate relevant instrumentation. Analyze and interpret experimental data, summarize findings, and propose next steps in collaboration with your supervisor and project team.
Perform independent laboratory work under appropriate supervision, including troubleshooting and optimizing experimental procedures.
Provide recommendations on experimental design, instrumentation, or process improvements that may enhance robustness, efficiency, or scalability.
Participate in regular check-ins, presenting progress and results to your supervisor and cross-functional stakeholders.
Rigorously document experimental plans, procedures, and results in laboratory notebooks, maintaining high standards and data integrity.
Present final project results in an oral presentation summarizing your project objectives, methods, results, and key learnings to R&D colleagues and the intern community.

Education: Currently enrolled in a STEM field such as chemistry, biology, biochemistry, chemical engineering, pharmaceutical science, molecular biology, microbiology, biomedical engineering, or other related fields
Degree: Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD
Academic Progress: Students must return to a degree seeking program for the fall semester following the completion of the internship.
Technical Skills and Core Competencies: Experience with hands-on laboratory work grained through independent research, teaching labs, or prior internship experience.
Comfort working at the bench (e.g., pipetting, solution preparation, aseptic technique, basic instrumentation) and following written protocols.
Basic proficiency with Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint for data organization, analysis, and presentation.
Scientific curiosity and a desire to innovate. Strong learning agility and willingness to acquire new techniques and concepts quickly.
Demonstrated critical thinking and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work effectively in team environments and communicate clearly with technical and non-technical colleagues
What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications):
Academic Progress: Expected graduation date between December 2027 and August 2028 with intention of entering industry following degree completion.
Research Experience: Sustained performance (>1 semester) in an undergraduate or graduate STEM research laboratory (academic, industry, or prior internship/co-op) with demonstrated technical growth.
Area-Specific Experience (depending on interest and placement):Synthetic/Analytical Development: Organic synthesis, route scouting, analytical method development, chromatography, spectroscopy, physicochemical characterization, or solid form characterization.
Formulation Development: Experience preparing dosage forms (e.g., solutions, suspensions, tablets, injectables), working with excipients, or conducting stability and compatibility studies. Experience with synthetic molecules, peptides, or biologics.
Bioprocess/Upstream Development: Mammalian or microbial cell culture, aseptic technique, bioreactor operation, media/feed preparation, process optimization, or scale up studies.
Antibody/Biologics: Immunoassays (e.g., ELISA), protein expression and purification, molecular cloning, flow cytometry, or related techniques.
Familiarity with statistical or data analysis tools (e.g., R, JMP, Python, Minitab, or similar) and/or data management systems.
Ability to work exceptionally well both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team, with appropriate levels of supervision.
Demonstrated interest in animal health, sustainability, veterinary medicine, or data driven approaches to R&D.
Strong written and oral communication skills, including the ability to clearly present scientific results.
Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced research environment.

Flexibility in geographic location.

Job Description
The Future Talent Program features internships that last up to 12 weeks and include working on one or more specially designed projects. These opportunities in our Research & Development Division provide meaningful professional development and an opportunity to explore whether our company is the right fit for your long-term career goals.
The Biocatalysis group within the Small Molecule Process Research & Development Department at our company is seeking motivated candidates to contribute to the invention, development, and innovative implementation of biocatalysts to advance the company's pipeline and impact on the scientific community. The candidates will work alongside company scientists in a laboratory environment to impact our drug discovery, development, and manufacture in the following key areas: biocatalysis, enzyme engineering, microfluidics, and fermentation. The role will involve the development of novel approaches, novel proteins, and enzyme-catalyzed reactions to enable access to biologically active compounds and chemical reactions relevant to the synthesis of drug-like molecules.
Day-to-day research for the intern will focus on solving key challenges in: (a) biocatalysis, which is the development of novel enzymatic transformations and expansion of biocatalytic toolbox to solve complex chemistry problems, (b) enzyme engineering, which is the design and engineering of proteins with novel functions, (c) microfluidics, screening and platform development including laboratory automation, data science, modeling and informatics, (d) fermentation, designing and executing improved methods to ensure robust enzyme production, and more! Candidates will leverage their chemistry, biology, engineering and/or analytical expertise to solve complex technical problems while working in both chemistry and biology laboratory spaces. The internship will provide an opportunity to gain firsthand knowledge on how our Research Labs develops and uses technologies to progress medicines and vaccines.
Interns will participate in departmental and project team meetings to provide a broad perspective on the drug discovery or development process in the pharmaceutical industry. Interns will also gain skillsets via exposure to practical aspects and day-to-day problems of pharmaceutical research. Interns will be responsible for and trained in methods for accurate electronic notebook recording and safe laboratory practices. In addition, they will have an opportunity to present their research results in both oral and written formats.
**Please note when applying for this position, if the candidate is selected for an interview, the applicant must be prepared to submit letters of recommendation and a brief research statement and a copy of transcripts.
Required Education & Experience:
Candidates must be a currently enrolled sophomore, junior, or senior student pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biological Sciences, Chemical Engineering, Bioengineering or Material Science; OR a currently a enrolled graduate student pursuing a Master's or Ph. D. in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biological Sciences, Chemical Engineering, Bioengineering or Material Science.
Candidates must have completed at least two years of study toward a bachelor’s degree by June 2027.
Candidates must be available to work full-time for approximately 11-12 weeks from beginning in May or June 2027.
Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States. Sponsorship from the company is not available for this role.
Preferred Experience & Skills:
Candidates should have a significant interest in organic chemistry, enzymology, protein design, directed evolution, chemical engineering or bioengineering, and/or high throughput screening. Molecular biology, synthetic biology, and materials science and engineering are also relevant disciplines.
Candidates should have basic laboratory skills and research experiences such as the use of lab notebook recording and safe lab practices.
Candidates should have experience and/or exposure to chemistry laboratory set-up techniques for multiple unit operations, including but not limited to reactions, workups (including liquid-liquid extraction), use of vacuum evaporation devices, and multiple purification techniques such as thin-layer chromatography, flash chromatography, crystallization, and precipitation.
Candidates should have experience and/or exposure to the use of analytical techniques and data interpretation such as high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, mass spectrometry (MS), and spectrophotometric techniques.
Candidates should have experience and/or exposure to fermentation process development, including both upstream and downstream unit operations.
Candidates should have experience and/or exposure to polymerase chain reaction (PCR) techniques, biochemical assays, and data analysis.
Candidates should have experience and/or exposure to programming languages including Python or MATLAB and (structural) data visualization tools.
Candidates should have a GPA of 3.0 or higher (preferred)
To learn more about the PRD team, click: Join Our Process Research & Development Team

Early Careers at nVent

Mechanical Engineering Co-op Program
The Mechanical Engineering Co-op Program with nVent’s Electrical Connections (EC) Business is a structured experiential learning program that gives students the opportunity to couple their academic knowledge with practical situations in the workplace, and simultaneously allows nVent to evaluate students as potential direct-hire talent. The Program is rotational between various departments, including Product Engineering, Product Development, Manufacturing, Labs and Compliance, and Digital Media Development. It is designed to engage students in the entire engineering process from development, through testing and applications, and to production. Students are assigned rotations and projects based on their academic levels and engineering capabilities and are given opportunities to champion these projects to completion and make significant contributions to existing processes. Our candidates are hands-on problem-solvers who are analytical, creative, and highly professional. We seek confident leaders who take the initiative to drive results.
Depending on the degree and/or desired career path, co-ops will be placed into some combination of the following rotations. 
Applications Engineering: Co-ops work within a team of engineers who design and implement new products within existing product lines. Responsibilities may include: 
Performing engineering calculations to analyze product designs for functionality and specification accuracy 
Assisting with resolution of technical issues related to product design, system design, and compliance with industry standards 
Participating in site visits and working with end-user customers 
Participating and presenting in design review meetings 
Using 2D and 3D modeling software to create and maintain engineering documentation
New Product Development: Co-ops gain exposure to new product design by participating in the conceptualization and development of innovative new products or modifications to existing products. Co-ops will learn the art of balancing engineering design, functional requirements, customer needs, and aesthetic appeal. Responsibilities may include: 
Fabricating and evaluating product concepts 
Assisting in creation of detailed drawings, 3D models, schematics, specifications, installation instructions, assembly prints, and test reports 
Utilizing analytical tools including Finite Element Analysis (ABAQUS) and Matlab 
Participating in site and supplier visits 
Participating and presenting in design review meetings 
Labs and Product Approvals: Co-ops build and support test programs for EFS products. Responsibilities may include: 
Developing test plans to verify product design intent 
Supporting efforts to ensure product compliance with codes and standards 
Procuring and assembling materials, and conducting validation testing 
Designing and improving test fixturing 
Gaining hands- on experience using various prototyping equipment (3D prints, CNC, Laser cutter, etc.) 
Co-op Program Benefits:    
We value the opportunity to develop students' knowledge of our business, and offer a valuable benefits to our co-ops including -
Opportunities to work alongside company and industry leaders possessing top educational and career credentials, as well as diverse backgrounds and experiences
Rotation between several engineering departments and nVent Electrical Connections manufacturing facilities to experience the entire engineering process from development to production
Interaction and collaboration with global teams
Opportunity to practice classroom theories, and use experiences gained in the work environment to inform class choices and career goals
Competitive hourly pay for time worked at an hourly rate of $25.00.
Relocation and housing support is available for eligible candidates  
Co-ops receive paid time off, paid sick time, paid volunteer time, and paid holidays 
Co-ops who demonstrate outstanding performance may be offered a subsequent internship/co-op or full-time offer of employment with nVent

Job Location

Job Description
Research and Development (R&D) at Procter & Gamble, the largest consumer packaged goods company in the world, includes a diverse group of roles that contribute to the innovation and development of our products. It encompasses roles in product research, formulation, testing, and scientific analysis. You will find variety and excitement starting Day 1.
This internship is specifically designed for individuals working towards a PhD who are developing proficiency in their field. As an intern or co-op in management, you will have the opportunity to learn from experienced professionals in a supportive environment. This is a 12-week paid internship, designed to provide you with a solid foundation for future career growth. The internship will take place from May (potentially early June) to August of 2027. Join us at P&G, where your contributions will play a vital role in shaping the future of consumer products!
The Opportunity:
P&G has an opportunity for a PhD intern to work in our Corporate R&D to develop an AI-agent-driven framework that automates and accelerates machine learning experimentation for time-series data modeling. The intern will explore how AI agents can propose and execute experiments, modify configurations or code, analyze results, and recommend next steps. This work will investigate improvements in data preprocessing, model architecture, training strategies, and hyperparameter selection while comparing AI-driven research with conventional experimentation in terms of model performance, reproducibility, and research efficiency.
The ideal candidate will demonstrate a strong eagerness to learn and grow professionally and possess excellent communication skills—both written and verbal. This role is perfect for those with passion for innovation and problem-solving, along with a proactive attitude and the ability to adapt to new challenges. Join us in this dynamic environment, where your contributions will make a real impact as part of a collaborative team!
Key Responsibilities:
Review existing literature and techniques in LLM-based AI agents, automated machine learning, and AI-enabled research systems.

The program runs 10 weeks, full time, beginning May 17, 2027, with internships hosted in Greenville, SC and Clearwater, FL.
Each internship is aligned to a department and business function, giving students the opportunity to apply classroom learning to real corporate projects in reporting, analysis, risk, and people operations. Interns will build professional networks through senior leader speaker sessions, peer engagement events, job shadowing, and exposure to the business operations behind a global IT distribution company.
Applications for the 2027 Summer Internship Cohort will close at 11:59 PM on Sunday, January 3rd. Students are encouraged to submit their materials early to ensure full consideration.
What We Are Looking For
Pursuing a business-related major, including Accounting, Finance, Economics, Human Resources or Human Capital Management, Business Administration, Risk Management, Management Information Systems, or a related field
Current undergraduate student with junior standing or above by summer 2027, including May 2027 graduates
Authorized to work in the United States without current or future sponsorship
Available to work full time, 40 hours per week, for the full 10-week program
Able to work from one of the listed locations on a hybrid schedule of three plus days per week in office
Proficient in Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook, with comfort building and working in spreadsheets
Preferred: familiarity with AI tools, such as Microsoft Copilot, and an interest in using technology to improve reporting accuracy and business outcomes
Detail orientation and comfort working with numbers, documentation, and confidential information
Interest in contributing to a values-driven culture guided by Together, We Own It; We Dare to Go; We Grow and Win; and We Do the Right Thing
Example Duties and Projects
Accounting Intern
Assist with core accounting activities, including journal entries, invoice processing, and account reconciliations
Support monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting, including participation in month-end and year-end close processes
Help maintain accurate ledgers and accounting records while contributing to audits and ad hoc business projects
Example project: support a month-end close process for a business unit, identify inefficiencies, and recommend process improvements
Finance Intern
Process vendor transactions accurately and on schedule while following internal controls
Collaborate with vendors and internal teams to research invoice discrepancies and support timely payment resolution
Reconcile vendor accounts and review aged receivables to help maintain account health and reduce financial risk
Maintain documentation and vendor records to support audit readiness and operational accuracy
Example project: complete a vendor account reconciliation, validate invoice activity, resolve discrepancies, and present recommendations to improve process efficiency and vendor relationships
Credit Intern
Review new account credit applications and evaluate creditworthiness using financial documentation and internal systems
Support fraud detection and risk mitigation by identifying potential concerns in credit applications
Partner with credit analysts to support decision-making and recommend appropriate credit terms
Example project: support a credit application workflow from document review and fraud screening through final recommendation, then present findings and efficiency opportunities
Supply Chain Intern
Support supply chain operations, from inventory planning and order management through distribution and delivery
Analyze inventory, order, and shipment data to identify trends and opportunities to improve efficiency
Partner with teams across the business and external suppliers to coordinate product flow and resolve operational challenges
Apply attention to detail to improve inventory accuracy, timely delivery, and the customer experience
Example project: own a supply chain improvement project from research and analysis through rollout, then present results such as time savings, reduced costs, or improved delivery performance
Events Intern
Support corporate and vendor events end to end, from planning and logistics through onsite execution
Build and send internal promotional communications that drive registration and engagement for events
Partner with teams across the business and with external vendor partners to coordinate event details
Apply attention to attendee experience and event design, the details that make an event memorable
Example project: own an event operations project from research and outreach through rollout, then present time savings and engagement results
Selected interns will complete a background check before the program begins.
Housing may be available in Greenville, SC, for eligible students

Experience firsthand what it’s like to lead a retail team within a Target store. This internship is a paid 40 hr/week, hands-on training program to develop and prepare you for store leadership. As a Stores Executive Intern, you will get a valuable realistic preview of the Executive Team Leader role (Assistant Store Manager) over a defined period of time. Within this store management internship, you will work closely with other managers and team members to develop an understanding of how Target’s retail business works and what it takes to excel in a management role. This program is designed to teach individuals how to lead within a retail store and you will:
Learn how to drive guest experience and impact your store’s financial, team, and operational performance.
Work alongside a mentor and learn how they effectively lead their department within the store.
Have the opportunity to step into leading your mentor’s departments- of course, we will be there to guide you and help you learn along the way!
Spend your days learning to lead and motivate a team, drive sales results, merchandise products, and provide an exceptional experience for our guests.
Have ongoing development conversations, as your development will be a top priority of ours.
Lead and support the execution of daily operations by working with your team members to build culture and guide your team to grow and achieve goals.

Overview:
The University of Virginia’s media relations team, which is part of Office of University Communications, is looking to hire a thoughtful, detail-oriented student colleague, who will lead the production cycle of our twice-weekly media newsletter, which reaches thousands of journalists.
This opportunity sits at the intersection of legacy media and emerging media, offering direct experience into the constantly evolving nature of university media relations in the digital era. This position will own the creation and execution of the newsletter, including helping the media relations team to refine its design and delivery. Beyond publishing each edition, this role will support strategic email list management and subscriber development. In totality, those responsibilities and opportunities offer a student internship role with nearly limitless potential.
This position is great for someone who enjoys refining processes over time and delivering work on a consistent cadence. While an interest in journalism and media is valuable, this position is best suited to candidates with a passion in high-quality execution, the strategic aspects of email communications, audience growth, and understanding how digital content reaches and engages with varying audiences.
You will be joining a small but determined Earned Media Team, where our mission is harnessing strategic media coverage to benefit the public and elevate the standing of world-class UVA experts. Our work directly supports UVA’s role as a public institution that serves all citizens of Virginia.
The starting date and weekly schedule are both highly flexible. In addition, the location of the work is highly flexible, hybrid in nature, and adaptable to student schedules. Optimal combination of remote-work arrangements and a vibrant, engaging office setting.
Key Responsibilities:
Produce and distribute the twice-weekly UVA Media Advisory newsletter, including drafting, editing, formatting, and quality assurance.
Maintain and improve the health of our media contact listserv by researching, adding, organizing, and removing contacts as needed.
Monitor engagement trends and recommend ideas to improve newsletter performance and user experience.
Brainstorm and test creative ways to make content easier for journalists to scan, discover relevant stories, and connect with our team for interview opportunities.
Work across a broad array of UVA experts and topic areas.
While not a responsibility, this role carries the opportunity to contribute to University Communications’ broader overall strategy and content.
Qualifications:
Currently enrolled as a full-time student at the University of Virginia.
Passionate long-term interest in the mission of public universities and how that mission intersects with public relations, digital marketing, communications, and the role of journalism in our society’s health and vibrance.
Demonstrated track record of drawing energy from the work of regular production cycles.
Basic proficiency or ability to learn email marketing software (Marketing Cloud, MailChimp, etc.)
Committed collaborator who gravitates toward team settings.
Preferred Qualifications:
Experience with email marketing platforms (Marketing Cloud, Mailchimp, etc.)
Experience creating newsletters, editorial content, or strategic messaging for varying audiences.
Interest in journalism, media relations, and academic research.
Scheduling: Digital marketing intern expected to work approximately 20 hours per week.
Compensation: $20/hr.

Please submit a resume and a brief cover letter outlining your interest in the position. Please limit the cover letter to 400 words. This application will remain open until we find our next teammate. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS
Resume and Cover Letter required.
Education: Current undergraduate and graduate UVA student
Experience: None
Licensure: None

This is primarily a sedentary job involving extensive use of desktop computers. The job does occasionally require traveling some distance to attend meetings, and programs.

The job details are as follows:
Who We Are
We are the first publicly-traded biotech or pharmaceutical company to take the form of a public benefit corporation. Our public benefit purpose is to provide a brighter future for patients through the development of novel pharmaceutical therapies; and technologies that expand the availability of transplantable organs.
United Therapeutics (Nasdaq: UTHR) seeks to travel down the corridors of indifference to develop treatments for rare, deadly diseases. We were founded in 1996 by a family seeking a cure for their daughter’s pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Today, we have six FDA-approved therapies that treat PAH, pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease (PH-ILD) and neuroblastoma, a rare pediatric cancer. Our near-term pipeline seeks to develop additional therapies for PAH and pulmonary fibrosis (PF).
The cure for end-stage life-threatening diseases like PAH, PH-ILD, PF, and many others is an organ transplant, but only a small percentage of donated organs are available to address the vast need. For this reason, we are working to create manufactured organs to address the shortage of kidneys, hearts, lungs, and livers available for transplant. We believe an unlimited supply of tolerable, transplantable organs will eliminate the transplant waiting list and cure end-stage organ diseases for which transplant is not currently an option.
The selected Co-op will need to be onsite at the RTP, North Carolina lab for the entire duration of this co-op role, from January 2027 through June of 2027.
Who You Are
Some co-ops fetch coffee. This one explores the future of lung science. Join our team and spend your spring tackling meaningful research projects in regenerative medicine, working with advanced imaging, cell culture, data analysis, and tissue engineering technologies. You'll learn from experts, contribute to discoveries that matter, and gain the kind of hands-on experience that can shape an entire scientific career.
This Spring 2027 Co-op will conduct and assist in research & development efforts to develop novel cell- and tissue-based products for treating pulmonary hypertension and other lung diseases.
This role will complete a focused research project to address a question that is relevant to the development of a cell- or tissue-based product for the treatment of lung disease(s). Generate data that addresses an insightful question and produce summary conclusions and report(s) to document the outcomes of experimental testing. Present data to management, team leaders, and research staff during internal review meetings, and make a final presentation of project findings.
The project will be chosen based upon the background of the applicant as well as the needs of the research & development team. Examples of R&D projects include:
Use in vitro tools to investigate how primary lung cells isolated from different donors behave uniquely.
Analyze transcriptomic data generated from lung cells and recellularized lung tissue.
Perform advanced imaging studies to visualize the microvasculature of the lung.
Minimum Requirements
Candidates are expected to be actively enrolled in an educational program toward the completion of a master’s or PhD in biology, biomedical sciences, engineering or related field for the duration of the co-op position
Must be available to work 40 hours/week onsite in the RTP, NC facility
Relevant coursework and laboratory experience
2+ years’ experience in cell culture
Experience with standard office software
Preferred Requirements
Specific experience or training required will vary depending on the project demands. Some projects may require:Experience with cell-based in vitro assays (e.g. tube formation, 3D hydrogels, microfluidics, application of shear stress, ALI)
Experience with cell analytical assays (e.g. flow cytometry, immunostaining, protein/mRNA characterization), such as 1-2 semesters of class/lab-work or academic/industry work experience
Experience with tissue handling and manipulation (ex vivo organ or tissue analysis techniques)
Experience with fluorescence microscopy; confocal microscopy, micro-CT or other 3D imaging experience strongly preferred
Large data analysis (e.g. RNA-seq, proteomics) and/or programming experience
Knowledge of lung biology or physiology, such as 1-2 semesters of class/lab-work and prior work/research in a pulmonary field
Experience required will vary depending upon the project/team needs, which may include:Microsoft Office (Excel, Powerpoint, Word)
Data analysis programs (e.g. Graphpad Prism, MATLAB)
Image analysis tools (e.g. ImageJ)
Coding languages (e.g. Python, C++, R)
Job Location
This position is located 100% onsite at our RTP, NC facility from January to June 2027.

This role is responsible for supporting professional employees working in an organizational function related to the Intern's area of study. Depending on the internship assignment, the intern may work alongside engineers, scientists, or industry professionals to contribute to various projects related to their area of study. Under guided supervision, interns will assist with various projects and tasks, contributing to the organization's goals while learning from experienced professionals in the field.
Please note: This is a pipeline requisition for anticipated Summer 2027 internship openings. We accept and review applications on a rolling basis, and we extend offers as individual positions are finalized and specific team hiring needs are confirmed. Submitting an application places you in consideration for upcoming opportunities as they open.
What You'll Do
Support active engineering projects and analyses within your area of study, contributing to work that advances real reactor design and licensing efforts.
Assist with the day-to-day technical and operational needs of your team.
Conduct research, gather technical data, and synthesize findings to inform ongoing design and analysis initiatives.
Help develop reports, technical documentation, and presentations that communicate results to internal stakeholders.
Organize and maintain project files, technical records, and documentation to support traceability and quality.
Participate actively in team meetings, design reviews, and brainstorming sessions — bringing ideas, asking questions, and offering perspective.
What You'll Bring
Current enrollment in — or recent completion of — a degree in mechanical engineering or a closely related field from an accredited institution.
Academic or hands-on knowledge in a minimum of one of the following areas:Mechanical Design
Designing and developing mechanical or fluid systems, assemblies, or components.
One plus years of demonstrated hands-on experience developing and delivering hardware or manufacturing processes in a production environment is required. May include industry internship experience, hobby, or participation in collegiate engineering projects such as: Formula SAE, Baja SAE, Design Build Fly, Rocket Club, etc.
Hardware ownership including manufacturing and testing oversight.
Use of Computer-Aided Design (CAD) and product lifecycle management (PLM) software.
Thermodynamics
Use of 1D flow-solvers performing heat/energy and mass balance (e.g., RELAP, Flownex, NPSS, SINDA/FLUINT, Flomaster, or similar).
E.g. UG/NX, SolidWorks, Pro-Engineer, Teamcenter, Windchill, or similar.
Structural Analysis
Analytical experience with structural analysis hand calculations and structural FEA software programs (e.g., ANSYS, ABAQUS, NASTRAN, FEMAP, CAESAR, ROHR, LS-DYNA, PIPESTRESS).
Thermal Hydraulics
Use of Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) analysis codes (e.g., STAR-CCM+, Fluent, or similar).
Mechanical Process Equipment
Piping, Ducting, HVAC, Fire Suppression, Pumps, Valves
Proficiency with the Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
Curiosity, initiative, and a collaborative mindset — you're eager to learn and ready to contribute.
Application Requirements
Along with your resume, please submit at least one letter of recommendation. Letters should come from a professor, academic advisor, employer, or professional mentor who can speak directly to your qualifications, work ethic, and potential.
